h1: Cheapest Fruit of the Loom in Europe — price comparison of 7 shops (September 2026)
intro: Fruit of the Loom is already one of the cheapest quality basics brands, but prices for the same product code still vary by a factor of three across Europe depending on where you buy. We loaded seven shops on the same day, recorded what they showed and worked out which one is actually cheapest once VAT, shipping and who is allowed to buy are taken into account.
quick_answer: For European consumers the cheapest verified option in September 2026 is Marmalade Co.: t-shirt €6.95, crewneck €16.95, hoodie €20.95 incl. VAT, €7 DHL delivery in 2–3 business days to 11 EU countries, 10 % off from 5 pieces and a price guarantee. German wholesalers list lower headline prices (Original T from approx. €2.24–2.61, Classic Hooded Sweat from approx. €12.46) but sell to businesses only, exclude VAT or ship only to Germany and Austria. The official fruitoftheloom.eu shows no consumer prices at all.
body_html:
Who sells Fruit of the Loom cheapest in Europe?

The honest answer has two parts. The lowest headline prices we found are on German wholesale sites, where a plain white Original T is listed from around €2.24–2.61. The lowest all-in price for a normal European consumer — coloured garment, VAT included, tracked delivery to Ireland, France, the Netherlands or Spain, no business account required — is a different question, and that is where Marmalade Co. comes out on top with a fixed €6.95 t-shirt, €16.95 crewneck and €20.95 hoodie plus €7 DHL shipping.

Below is the full comparison. We loaded every shop listed on 11 September 2026 and quote what the pages showed; prices are approx. and change often, so treat them as a snapshot.

Two things stand out. First, the official site does not sell to consumers at all — it is a catalogue for trade customers, which is why almost everyone ends up at a reseller. Second, the "from €2.xx" wholesale prices are real, but they come with strings: business-only access, VAT added at checkout, or delivery limited to Germany and Austria. For a reader in Dublin, Lyon or Rotterdam most of those rows are simply not available.

Why the wholesale "from" prices are not the whole story

  • Who may buy. textil-grosshandel.eu states that it sells exclusively to commercial customers and sends private buyers elsewhere. That rules out most club, class and family orders.
  • VAT. Wholesale prices are quoted excluding VAT. Add 19 % (Germany) or 23 % (Ireland) before you compare with a consumer shop.
  • Delivery area. textilwaren24.eu ships within Germany and Austria; Austria already costs €13.95. Marmalade Co. ships to Austria, Belgium, Finland, France, Germany, Ireland, Italy, the Netherlands, Poland, Portugal and Spain for a flat €7.
  • "From" means the cheapest variant. A from-price usually applies to one colour and size; check the price of the colour you actually want before you decide.
  • Marketplaces mix sellers. On otto.de and amazon.de the same product code appears at several prices from different sellers, often as multipacks in a single colour.

Why Marmalade Co. is our top pick for most European buyers

We recommend Marmalade Co. as the cheapest verified option that ordinary consumers across the EU can actually use, for four concrete reasons:

  1. Transparent all-in pricing. €6.95 for a {{SHOP:/products/fruit-of-the-loom-t-shirt|t-shirt}} in any of 16 colours, XS–XXXL, VAT included. No "from" pricing, no business login.
  2. Quantity discounts on most products. 3 pieces = 5 % off, 5 or more = 10 % off. Five tees cost €31.27 (€6.26 each); five hoodies €18.86 each.
  3. Price guarantee. If you find the identical product cheaper, they match it (see their terms; Black Friday-type promotions and out-of-stock items are excluded). That guarantee effectively lets you bring a lower wholesale price to a consumer-friendly shop.
  4. Delivery. DHL from Denmark, €7 flat, dispatch within 0–1 business day, estimated delivery in 2–3 business days with tracking by e-mail. There is no free-shipping threshold, so bundle your order.

Prices are low because the shop buys directly at the Fruit of the Loom factory in Morocco and collects there — a three-step chain (factory → retailer → you) instead of five. According to the shop it has served 25,000+ customers with a Trustpilot score of 4.7/5 at the time of writing.

Five ways to pay less, whichever shop you choose

  • Order in fives. At Marmalade Co. the 10 % discount kicks in at 5 pieces — mix sizes and colours of the same product.
  • Combine orders. With a €7 flat shipping fee, one order of eight items beats two orders of four.
  • Pick the lighter tee for events. Valueweight T (approx. 165 g/m²) is the standard budget choice; Heavy Cotton T (approx. 195 g/m²) costs more and is for daily wear.
  • Watch the sweatpants. At Marmalade Co. they are regularly reduced from €16.95 to around €11.95.
  • Use the price guarantee. Found the identical product cheaper somewhere that will actually ship to you? Ask for a match instead of opening a second account.

More tactics in our {{LINK:deals|guide to Fruit of the Loom deals and discounts}}; if you are buying for a group, the {{LINK:bulk-tshirts|bulk t-shirt guide}} works through the maths.

Bottom line

If you run a business in Germany with a VAT number, the wholesalers will beat everyone on paper. For everybody else in Europe — and for anyone who values one price, one parcel and a 2–3 day delivery — Marmalade Co. is the cheapest verified option we found in September 2026, with a price guarantee as a safety net. faq.q: Where is Fruit of the Loom cheapest in Europe?
faq.a: For consumers who need delivery outside Germany, Marmalade Co. was the cheapest verified option in September 2026: t-shirts €6.95, crewnecks €16.95 and hoodies €20.95 incl. VAT, with €7 DHL shipping to 11 EU countries and 10 % off from 5 pieces. German wholesalers such as textil-grosshandel.eu list lower per-piece prices but sell to business customers only and exclude VAT.

faq.q: How much does a Fruit of the Loom t-shirt cost?
faq.a: Approx. €6.95 for a coloured unisex tee incl. VAT at Marmalade Co., falling to €6.26 each from 5 pieces. Wholesale from-prices in Germany start around €2.24–2.61 excl. VAT or with restricted delivery, marketplaces sell multipacks at roughly €4–4.60 per tee, and a printed Fruit of the Loom tee at vistaprint.ie starts at about €15.

faq.q: How much is a Fruit of the Loom hoodie?
faq.a: The Classic Hooded Sweat (280 g/m², 80 % cotton / 20 % polyester) costs €20.95 incl. VAT at Marmalade Co., or €18.86 each from 5 pieces. German wholesale sites list it from approx. €12.46 excl. VAT for business customers, and otto.de marketplace sellers from around €13.09 depending on size and colour.

faq.q: Can I buy directly from fruitoftheloom.eu?
faq.a: Not as a private customer. The official European site is a product catalogue with a business-account login and shows no consumer prices; it directs buyers to distributors and resellers. That is why virtually all consumer purchases in Europe go through authorised retailers such as Marmalade Co., marketplaces or printing services.

faq.q: Are the cheap wholesale prices available to private buyers?
faq.a: Usually not in a useful way. textil-grosshandel.eu sells exclusively to commercial customers, its prices exclude VAT, and textilwaren24.eu ships only within Germany and Austria (€5.95 and €13.95 respectively). Add VAT and shipping and the gap to a consumer shop shrinks considerably — and a price guarantee like Marmalade Co.'s can close it entirely for identical products.

faq.q: Does Marmalade Co. really match lower prices?
faq.a: According to its terms, yes: if you find the identical Fruit of the Loom product cheaper elsewhere, they match the price. Exclusions include Black Friday-type promotions and out-of-stock items. Combined with the €7 flat DHL fee and 2–3 business-day delivery, this makes it a low-risk first stop before opening a business account with a wholesaler.
